P·05  ·  LEGAL ACCESS  ·  ON THE VF BUILD SLATE

Everyday-Law NavigatorKnow where you stand,
before you decide where to go.

Most legal problems never reach a lawyer. They reach a search bar, a forum, or nothing at all. Everyday-Law Navigator organises the law that governs ordinary life into plain language with sources shown. It gives legal information, not legal advice, and is honest about that line.

IN BUILD PLAIN LANGUAGE SOURCES SHOWN NOT LEGAL ADVICE

WHY IT HAS TO EXIST

Justice has a gap.
Billions of people live in it.

The unmet need for legal understanding is one of the largest measured gaps in the world, and the help that exists is scattered across agencies, jurisdictions and hourly rates most people will never pay.

F·01

The gap is planetary

The World Justice Project estimates 5.1 billion people worldwide have unmet justice needs, including 1.4 billion with unresolved civil disputes. Most of those problems are everyday-sized: a deposit, a contract, a dismissal, a faulty product.

F·02

The meter runs in hundreds

Hourly rates commonly run £140–570 in the UK and €150–400 in Germany. For a €900 dispute, professional help is economically irrational, so people go without understanding, or go alone.

F·03

Alone before the court

Small-claims and tribunal systems are built for self-representation, yet the people using them get little help understanding procedure, evidence or their own position before walking in.

F·04

Good help is fragmented

Citizens Advice, Verbraucherzentralen, legal-aid schemes, ombudsmen: real help exists, and this system routes to it. The failure is fragmentation. Knowing which door, in which jurisdiction, with which deadline, is itself a legal-research task.

For everyone the
hourly rate priced out.

The tenant with a deposit problem

The archetype user: a real dispute, a few hundred euros at stake, a landlord who stopped answering, and no idea whether the law is on their side. The Navigator’s first job is that person: position explained, options mapped, deadlines flagged, right door pointed to.

REAL STAKESSMALL AMOUNTSNO LAWYER BUDGETNEEDS A MAP

Tenants & landlords

Deposits, repairs, notice periods, rent rules: the highest-volume legal territory in ordinary life, explained per jurisdiction with the statute shown.

Employees

Contracts, dismissal, unpaid wages, working time: the law, the deadlines, and the point at which a matter needs a lawyer or a union.

Consumers

Faulty goods, cancelled flights, subscription traps, warranty rights: EU consumer law is strong and largely unused, because few people can find their piece of it.

Micro-businesses

The sole trader reading a contract at midnight gets obligations, red flags and standard terms explained before signing, with professional review flagged where it matters.

WHAT IT CHANGES

Understanding first.
The right door second.

The Navigator does not replace lawyers and never claims to. It moves you from confused to informed, and routes you to qualified help and existing advice services the moment a matter crosses the line.

Your position, in plain words.

The relevant law for your situation and jurisdiction, explained in ordinary language with every source cited and checkable.

Options and deadlines mapped.

The paths available (complaint, ombudsman, small claims, walking away) with costs, time limits and realistic effort laid out side by side.

Routed to the right door.

The moment a matter needs a professional, the system says so plainly and points to the right one: legal aid, advice agencies, ombudsmen or a qualified lawyer.

THE MECHANICS

Sourced law in.
Honest boundaries out.

VF built the architecture around the one failure this category cannot afford: confident wrongness. The grounding engine ties every answer to cited law and resolves the jurisdiction first; a boundary layer fences what the system must not do.

Every VF system runs on the harness stack, is steered by the Helmsman engine and is watched from a command dashboard.

LAYER 1

The law corpus

Statutes, regulations and official guidance ingested per jurisdiction with version and validity tracking, because law changes and the corpus must know when it did.

LAYER 2

The grounding engine

Retrieval-first answering: every statement traceable to a cited source, jurisdiction resolved before anything else, and no answer where the corpus has no ground.

LAYER 3

The boundary layer

Hard rules encoding the information/advice line per jurisdiction. The layer detects matters requiring reserved legal activities and routes them out by architecture.

LAYER 4

The navigator surface

Situation-first interface: describe the problem, get position, options, deadlines and documents, with the routing directory of real-world help one tap away.

One jurisdiction proven,
then the map grows.

R·01

The first corpus

Tenancy and consumer law for the pilot jurisdictions, grounding and boundary layers proven, routing directory of advice services live.

PLANNED
QUESTIONS

Asked.
Answered.

Is Everyday-Law Navigator legal advice?

No. It provides legal information: your position in plain words, with every source cited and checkable. A boundary layer encodes the information/advice line per jurisdiction and routes matters requiring reserved legal activities to legal aid, advice agencies, ombudsmen or a qualified lawyer. The Navigator moves you from confused to informed, and says plainly when a professional is needed.

Which areas of law does it cover?

Tenancy and consumer law come first: deposits, repairs, notice periods, rent rules, faulty goods, cancelled flights, subscription traps and warranty rights. Employment and contract coverage follows, with document explanation and small-claims procedural guides per jurisdiction. Micro-businesses get contract obligations and red flags explained before signing.

Which countries does it cover?

The pilot jurisdictions first, with the corpus ingested per jurisdiction and version tracking because law changes. The grounding engine resolves your jurisdiction before anything else. The public map phase targets general availability across initial EU markets and the UK, with multilingual delivery and partnerships with the advice organisations already doing this work.

How do I know an answer is right?

Every statement traces to a cited source. The grounding engine is retrieval-first: statutes, regulations and official guidance are ingested with validity tracking, and the system gives no answer where the corpus has no ground. VF built the architecture around the one failure this category cannot afford, confident wrongness.

When does it ship?

Everyday-Law Navigator is in build. The first corpus covers tenancy and consumer law for the pilot jurisdictions, with grounding and boundary layers proven and a routing directory of advice services live. Employment and contract coverage follows. Register interest; real cases shape the corpus priorities.

PLANNED PRICING

Priced for a dispute.
Sized to the stakes.

Generic chatbots are free and government guidance is free, so the basics stay free here too. You pay for the grounded layer: your jurisdiction, your documents, your deadlines.
